skill.name: executing-epic-workflow
skill.description: Execute structured feature development with the EPIC workflow: Explore, Research, Plan, Validate, Implement, Review, and Iterate.
skill.summary: Guide complex feature work through phased research, planning, implementation, validation, review, and iteration.
skill.author: Emz1998

content.value_statement: Complex feature work can lose context, skip validation, and leave no audit trail. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code through a phased EPIC workflow with delegated research, planning, validation, review, and iteration.
actual_capabilities: Creates a numbered session directory pattern for each feature workflow.
Defines seven phases from exploration through final iteration.
Delegates exploration, research, planning, validation, review, testing, and troubleshooting to named agents.
Requires phase reports such as codebase status, research, plans, feedback, and quality review.
Runs a bundled validation script to check required report files.
Enforces retry loops when phase validation fails.
limitations: Validation checks file presence, not the quality or accuracy of report content.
Requires compatible agent delegation tools and writable project files.
May add overhead for small tasks that do not need formal phases.
Research quality depends on available sources and configured browsing permissions.

use_cases.title: Plan a Complex Feature
use_cases.description: A product engineer explores code, researches options, creates a plan, and validates it before implementation.

use_cases.title: Coordinate AI Subagents
use_cases.description: An AI tooling lead standardizes how Claude, Codex, or Claude Code assign research, review, and troubleshooting work.

use_cases.title: Document Delivery Evidence
use_cases.description: A team lead keeps phase reports that show decisions, quality checks, and final verification for a feature.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Basic EPIC Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the EPIC workflow for this feature: [feature]. Create the session directory, complete each phase, and show each validation result.

prompt_templates.title: Add Planning Depth
prompt_templates.prompt: Use EPIC for [feature]. Give extra focus to exploration, research, risks, trade-offs, and a clear implementation plan before writing code.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate Review and Tests
prompt_templates.prompt: Use EPIC for [feature]. After implementation, coordinate code review and testing validation, then address all high-priority findings before final verification.

prompt_templates.title: Recover a Failed Phase
prompt_templates.prompt: Continue the EPIC workflow in [session directory]. Identify the failed phase, regenerate missing reports, rerun validation, and proceed only after it passes.

output_examples.input: Build a billing settings page with audit logging.
output_examples.output: The workflow creates a session folder, gathers codebase context, researches billing patterns, plans implementation, validates the plan, implements changes, reviews quality, and records final verification.

output_examples.input: Add password reset emails and verify edge cases.
output_examples.output: Expected outputs include a research report, implementation plan, validation feedback, implementation summary, quality report, and final verification note.

output_examples.input: The review phase failed because the quality report is missing.
output_examples.output: The workflow reinvokes the review agent with an explicit save instruction, checks the required report, and repeats validation until the phase passes.

best_practices: Start with a narrow feature description and clear success criteria.
Review each generated phase report before moving to the next phase.
Run validation after every phase and resolve missing reports immediately.
anti_patterns: Using the workflow for a tiny edit that needs no research or plan.
Skipping validation because a report seems obvious.
Letting subagents write implementation code during non-implementation phases.

faq.question: What does EPIC mean in this skill?
faq.answer: EPIC means Explore, Research, Plan, Validate, Implement, Review, and Iterate.

faq.question: Does the skill write code automatically?
faq.answer: It guides the main agent to implement after exploration, research, planning, and plan validation are complete.

faq.question: Why does it create session files?
faq.answer: Session files keep phase reports, decisions, review findings, and final verification in one place.

faq.question: Can I use it for small fixes?
faq.answer: Yes, but it is usually better for complex work that needs research, planning, or review.

faq.question: What does the validation script check?
faq.answer: It checks that required report files exist for each phase. It does not judge report quality.

faq.question: Does it require specific subagents?
faq.answer: The workflow references named agents for exploration, research, planning, validation, review, testing, and troubleshooting.
